rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded, not just its header (§4's sibling).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-read at current wording (rule.js lectures 5) and re-run against the body with the rule's own named enforcement script: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <this file>` → 1 oversized slide, `## Sources` (L89) at 12 bullets against the ≤6 cap (12 one-line citation bullets, L93-L104 — matches the maintainer block's own "12 cites across 11 organisations" count). All 12 other `##` slides pass both axes. Judged PASS on harm, not on the raw count: §5's stated purpose is glance-legibility of a slide a reader takes in AS ONE IDEA under time pressure; a Sources list is not a concept slide, it is a flat reference list meant to be scanned for a name, not glanced-and-understood — the same "scanned rather than read" distinction check_slides.md §9 already draws by name for reading-list/menu slides on the adjacent bold-budget rule. Splitting the list at a "conceptual seam" (the fix §5 prescribes) does not apply to a flat citation list with no internal concept boundary, and an artificial split (Sources 1-6 / Sources 7-12) would degrade the lookup rather than aid it. No maintainer accept-note exists for this slide (checked maintainer block, none found) — flagged as a TODO, not carded as a REVISE, per the harm-absent clause: report as a rule question, not a fix.
